sentences.text: The facts, as emanating from the paper book, are that the appellant instituted a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short 'The MV Act') seeking compensation on account of injuries and permanent disability suffered by him in a motor vehicular accident which took place on 16.01.2016.

2.1 The case of the appellant was that on 16.01.2016, he along with his cousin was going to Village Bathlana on his Motorcycle, which was being driven by his cousin at a normal speed on the left side of the 1 of 8 FAO-4140-2022 (O&M) [2] road.
He was the pillion rider.

At about 6:40 p.m., when they reached near the shops of Village Bhago Majra, a car bearing temporary Regn. No.PB-65-Temp-1805 and Permanent registration No. PB-01A-8488 (hereinafter referred to as the "offending vehicle") driven by respondent No.1 (Manjit Singh) in a rash and negligent manner and at a high speed came from the village Bhago Majra and struck into the motorcycle of the appellant.
The appellant sustained multiple grievous injuries and suffered a fracture in his left leg, for which a rod was surgically inserted.
The appellant was taken to Chawla Hospital, Phase-7 Mohali, where he underwent treatment and contributed to remain under medical care.
2.2 FIR No.22, dated 19.01.2016 under Sections 279, 337, 338 IPC was lodged at Police Station Sohana against respondent No.1.

It was averred that the accident had taken place on account of the Taranveer Ladi vs Manjit Singh And Others on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72238191/

2.3 It was averred that at the time of the accident, the appellant was 14 years old and was a brilliant student of 10+1 class and an active sportsperson.
It was averred that his prospective income may be assessed at Rs. 15,000/- per month and claimant has incurred medical expenses to the tune of Rs. 4,50,000/- on his treatment.
Accordingly, a sum of Rs.20 lakhs was claimed as compensation.
3. Respondent no. 2 and 3 appeared before the Tribunal.
Respondent no. 1 initially appeared through counsel but failed to file a written statement and subsequently stopped appearing; therefore he was proceeded against ex-parte.
Respondents No. 2 (owner of the offending vehicle) filed a written statement.
The factum of the accident was 2 of 8 FAO-4140-2022 (O&M) [3] denied.

It was averred that a false FIR was got registered against respondent No.1.
3.2.
Respondent No.3 (National Insurance Company Ltd.) filed its separate written statement raising usual defences.
The factum of the accident was denied.
It was specifically pleaded that respondent no. 1, driver of the offending vehicle, was not holding a valid and effective driving licence at the time of the alleged accident.

4. From the pleadings of the parties, following issues were framed:
"1. Whether Taranveer Ladi had sustained injuries in a motor vehicular accident,
which took place on 16.01.2016 at about 6:40 P.M near shops of Bhago Majra,
Mohali, on account of rash and negligent driving of Tata Indigo bearing temporary registration No. PB-65-Temp-1805 now bearing No. PB-01-A-8488, driven by respondent No. 1 Manjit Singh ?
OPP 2.
If issue No. 1 is proved, whether claimant is entitled to receive the compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?
OPP 3.
Whether the claimant has no locus standi to file the claim petition?
OPR 4.
Whether respondent no. 1 was not having the valid and effective driving licence, at the time of accident, if so, its effect?

[4]
5. Whether the petition is not maintainable?
OPR-2 6. Relief."
5. Parties led their respective evidence.
6. On issue No.1, it was held that the accident had been caused on account of the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent No.1.

7. Aggrieved by the grant of inadequate compensation, the present appeal was preferred.
8. I have heard learned counsel for the parties.
9. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the compensation awarded by the MACT is grossly inadequate.

It is submitted that as a result of the injuries suffered in the accident, the left 4 of 8 FAO-4140-2022 (O&M) [5] leg of the appellant got shortened by 2" and the pain and suffering on account of the said disability shall continue for the whole life, but the said fact was not taken into consideration, while awarding the compensation.
It is further argued that the appellant remained hospitalized for a considerably long time and, thus, the amount awarded towards attendant charges and special diet, are very much on the lower side.
Learned counsel further argues that the amount awarded towards future prospects of marriage, is also on the lower side and the same deserves to be enhanced.

Apart from that it is also argued that in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Baby Sakshi Greola vs. Manzoor Ahmad Simon and another, 2024 SCC Online SC 3692, the MACT ought to have applied the multiplier of 18 instead of 15 while assessing the compensation.

It is further argued that the appellant being 14 years of age, assessment of such notional income is very much on the higher side.

It is also argued that even if the income of the appellant was assessed as per the minimum wages prevalent at the time of accident, then also it Taranveer Ladi vs Manjit Singh And Others on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72238191/

sentences.text: I have considered the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties and have also perused the record.
11.1. At the outset, it may be noticed that there is no challenge to the impugned award by respondent No.3-Insurance Company.
Thus, the factum of accident and the injuries and disability suffered by the appellant, in and/or as a result of the said accident, is not in dispute.
12. The appellant had suffered a permanent disability of 12% on account of shortening of his leg by 2".
The functional disability of the appellant was assessed at 25%.
The notional income was assessed as Rs.12,000/- per month.
It was claimed that the appellant wanted to go to the Indian Army, but on account of the disability suffered by him in the accident, he would not be able to do so.

13. In the considered opinion of this Court, the notional income of the appellant was assessed slightly on the higher side because the minimum wages at the relevant time were at best around Rs.8,000/- per month and even after adding 40%, as future prospects, the income would come to Rs.11,200/-.
However, in any case, this Court does not intend to interfere in the notional income, which was assessed as Rs.12,000/- per month.
14. Under the circumstances, there would be no change in the loss of future income as assessed by the MACT.

However, keeping in view the judgments of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Baby Sakshi Greola's case (supra) and Sudheesh M Vs. M.K.
Purushothaman and others, 2025 ACJ 2843 and Reshma Vs. Dajiba Krishna Lad and another, 2024(4) ACC 611, the compensation under the head of pain and suffering 6 of 8 FAO-4140-2022 (O&M) [7] and marriage prospects, deserves to be enhanced to Rs.2,00,000/- under each head.

Compensation on Rs. 25,000/- No change account of future medical expenses 7. Compensation on Rs. 20,000/- No change account of special diet 8. Compensation on Rs. 20,000/- No change account of transportation charges 9.
Compensation on Rs. 15,000/- No change account of attendant 10.

Compensation on Rs. 50,000/- Rs. 2,00,000/-
account of damages for pain, mental agony and amenities of life as a consequences of injuries 11.
Compensation on Rs. 50,000/- Rs. 2,00,000 account of marriage prospects 12.
The total compensation as enhanced by this Court, therefore, comes to Rs.10,90,000/-.
After deducting a sum of Rs.7,90,000/-, as assessed by the MACT, the balance compensation comes to Rs.3,00,000/- .
This amount would be payable in addition to the amount assessed by the 7 of 8 FAO-4140-2022 (O&M) [8] learned MACT along with interest @ 7.5% per cent annually.
The liability to pay the same would be as per the award.
15. The present appeal is accordingly disposed of.
Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand disposed of.
